cases.stated_intent: A foldable stand supports a laptop at eye level; no hinge/rail choice has been made.
cases.unresolved_question: Desired adjustment, stability and load conditions.

task_handoff.level_a_handoff: A Mechanical support concept the inventor can confirm: how the foldable stand, in its intended use configuration, rests on its surface and carries the laptop. Whether a simple two-support reaction calculation applies can be judged only once that support configuration is known, and it may not apply; withholding it until then is correct.
inventor_provided: the laptop is to be held at eye level
the stand folds
no hinge, sliding rail or other adjustment has been chosen
decision_relevant_unknowns: how the stand rests and carries the laptop (its support configuration)
where and how it is used, e.g. on a desk and whether the laptop is typed on
whether and how the height should be adjustable
missing_measurements: the laptop's weight, which the inventor can measure
the support spacing and the laptop's centre-of-gravity position, measurable only once a configuration exists
qualified_calculations: two-support static reactions, only if the configuration matches that method's declared conditions; the result would be unvalidated and would say nothing about strength, stiffness or tipping
admitted_references: prototype material families for a non-functional appearance mock-up only, not for a load-bearing stand

cases.stated_intent: A window that opens and closes by itself: a hinge arm swings the window and a small motor board switches battery power to a geared motor that turns the arm; how the two parts work together and how to check that it works are not yet worked out.
not_stated_or_not_verified: the motor can move the window
a specific motor, gearbox or board
cases.unresolved_question: How the two parts are meant to work together and what observable result would show that the window opens and closes as intended.

task_handoff.level_a_handoff: A preparation record for the ONE stated interaction between the Mechanical part (the hinge arm) and the Electrical / Electronics part (the motor board and geared motor): the intended operating conditions, an observable acceptance result and the evidence or check needed. Preparation only; no component choice and no compatibility judgement.
inventor_provided: the window should open and close by itself
a hinge arm swings the window
a small motor board switches battery power to a geared motor that turns the arm
how the parts work together and how to check it are not yet worked out
decision_relevant_unknowns: how the motor board, the geared motor and the hinge arm are meant to act on each other
the conditions it must work in, e.g. indoor or outdoor and how often it opens
what observable result would show that it opens and closes as intended
what check or evidence would show that result
missing_measurements: the force needed to open and close the window, which can be measured
the time to open and close
the battery current drawn, once a motor is chosen
qualified_calculations: the moment of one measured force about the hinge, only once that force and its lever arm are known; it is not a motor or torque requirement
admitted_references: basic electrical relations such as power equals voltage times current, as reference only and not as battery sizing or runtime
specialist_review: whether the motor can move the window and the parts are compatible
pinch and entrapment safety of an automatic window
